title: UP CEO Admits ECI Auto-generated 85,000+ Voter Deletion Forms Without a Reason, Confirms Mass Deletion Attempts Against Muslims
authors: Sumedha Mittal, Ayushi Kar (edited by Nitin Sethi)
shows: A follow-up to the Collective's investigation of 9 October 2026 into the 85,854 Form 7s that the Commission's software ERONET produced in Uttar Pradesh with no reason for deletion. It reports that the state's Chief Electoral Officer called the report misleading on X and in a recorded video, and that in the video he did not dispute the count or explain why the reasons were missing. It quotes him putting the names targeted by bulk Form 7s at about 4,700 among 13.39 crore electors, and reports that the Commission capped the number of deletion objections one person may file.
quote: Yet, in his video, Rinwa confirmed our finding that the ECI software had forced election officers in UP to sign 85,854 forms to delete voters without stating a reason.
He did not explain why most of the auto-generated forms did not mention any reason for deleting the voters.

“The total number of names against which [bulk] deletion complaints were made through these Form 7s was only about 4,700. In Uttar Pradesh, which has a population in crores and where we have 13.39 crore [voters]. They found only 4,700 such names where there were multiple Form 7s,” said Rinwa.
Instead, on October 9, it ordered that no person would be allowed to file more than 30 objections in a month for deletion of voters.

In his response to the said story, the UP CEO claimed there was no “irregularity” in the process because every voter deleted through these Form 7 submissions was sent a notice citing the ground for their hearing, that they were either unmapped or had “logical discrepancies” in their records.
note: Opened on 15 October 2026 (200, full text in the page). Byline Sumedha Mittal and Ayushi Kar, edited by Nitin Sethi, published and updated 14 October 2026, free to read. The first investigation (https://www.reporters-collective.in/trc/eci-software-auto-generated-forms-to-delete-without-reason, 9 October) is already in round3.json, so this is a separate follow-up. The subheading says the cap came 'Two days later', while the body dates the Commission's order 9 October. The figure '30 objections in a month' does not match PTI (ThePrint, 10 Oct 2026) and News On AIR (10 Oct 2026), which both report a cap of 10 Form 7s per elector for the claims and objections period and five a month in continuous updation, so 'shows' does not repeat the 30. The links to the CEO's X post and video in the article could not be followed from the saved page. The 13.39 crore in the quotation equals the site's UP final roll of 13,39,84,792 (data/uttarpradesh/summary.json, final).

title: In India, a Dark Shadow Falls on Its Vaunted Elections
shows: A lawyer's essay for an international readership on the protests in Delhi on 10 and 12 October 2026 and how the SIR reached them. It argues that the Supreme Court let the revision become a fact on the ground before ruling on it, then upheld it in 2026 without requiring the Commission to act proportionately, and that the Commission's independence was never secured in law. It cites the 90% of decided West Bengal appeals that restored the elector and the Indian Express investigation into the two Commissioners' objections.
quote: The SIR ostensibly seeks to clean up and update the electoral rolls but has removed 130 million Indians from the rolls—more than half the number of Americans eligible to vote in the midterm elections.
For months, the Supreme Court did not rule on the legality of electoral revisions on such a vast scale, allowing the exercise to become a fait accompli.
One indication of how flawed the SIR may have been was that around 90% of the voters in West Bengal, whose appeals were decided, were eventually restored to the rolls.
Eventually, when the Supreme Court finally issued its judgment in the summer of 2026, it upheld the entire exercise.

Two failures converged: the failure to entrench the Election Commission’s independence in law and in the Constitution, and the failure of the Supreme Court to intervene despite evidence of disenfranchisement placed before it.
note: Opened on 15 October 2026 (200, full text in the page). TIME Ideas section, by Gautam Bhatia, 'a lawyer and the author of The Indian Constitution: Conversations with Power'. datePublished 2026-10-13T11:45Z, no isAccessibleForFree flag and the text loaded without a paywall. It is opinion, so it is grouped with the law and the courts, where its argument lies. Two things for the second reader. The piece says the protest was on Saturday (10 October) with more than 7,000 detained, and that thousands protested again on Monday (12 October), which 'shows' gives as protests on 10 and 12 October. It follows the 90% figure with 'Nine out of every ten excluded voters had been wrongfully removed', which goes further than the figure (90% of decided appeals, not of all excluded voters), so 'shows' quotes the figure and leaves that sentence out. Its 130 million agrees with the site's 13,39,03,307 left off the drafts in 31 states (data/india/states.json, total.removed). Its 'nine million ... around 12%' for West Bengal is the paper's own and was not checked against data/westbengal.

title: Inside The Election Commission: Investigation Finds ECs Split On Key Issues | Indian Express Special
shows: The paper's video account of its investigation into the Election Commission. Two Election Commissioners objected on file at least 14 times in 10 months to decisions they said were taken without their knowledge, on deletions, additions, appeals and access to ERONET and ECINET. It also covers the questions added to Form 6, the 97 Goa electors officials could not restore, and the 16 lakh appeals the Commission told the Supreme Court were filed in West Bengal against restored voters.
quote: Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi formally objected at least 14 times over the past 10 months to decisions they said were taken without their knowledge or approval.

In West Bengal, 60 lakh voters were flagged for “logical discrepancies”, with 27 lakh subsequently deleted. The Election Commission later told the Supreme Court that 16 lakh appeals had also been filed against voters whose names had been restored by judicial officers.

The question is whether the process is lawful, decentralised, transparent and auditable — and whether the officials legally responsible for maintaining voter rolls actually have control over the systems they are expected to operate.

title: Election Commission Row: Is The SIR Process Legally Valid?

title: SIR: 8 Questions, 8 Clear Answers | Election Facts | BJP
shows: The BJP's own account of the SIR, answering eight questions the party lists as the 13 crore names, Form 6, ECINET, young voters, the role of the Election Commissioners, 'vote chori' and AI. Its description says the SIR is meant to include eligible voters and drop ineligible entries, with claims, objections and appeals, and gives Bihar's final roll as about 7.42 crore.
quote: From the alleged removal of 13 crore voters to questions around Form 6, ECINET, Gen Z voters, the role of Election Commissioners, Vote Chori and AI — this video examines eight major questions surrounding the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) and the electoral-roll process.

The Election Commission’s published material states that SIR is intended to ensure that eligible voters are included while ineligible entries are removed, with mechanisms for claims, objections and appeals. In Bihar’s 2025 SIR, the final roll included about 7.42 crore electors, after additions and deletions during the revision process.

title: “13 Crore Voters Deleted?”| The Real SIR Numbers Explained | #SIR | #BJP
shows: A BJP short on the 13 crore names left off the drafts. Its description splits them as the Commission did into absent, shifted or other (9.5 crore, 71%), dead (2.7 crore, 20%) and duplicate (1 crore, 7.6%), argues that calling all 13 crore genuine voters is wrong, and points to the Commission's drive to enrol eligible voters who were left out.
quote: “13 Crore Voters Deleted” — but what does this number actually include?
9.5 Crore+ (71%) — Absent, shifted or other categories
2.7 Crore+ (20%) — Deceased entries
1 Crore+ (7.6%) — Multiple/duplicate entries
Presenting the entire figure simply as “13 crore genuine voters deleted” does not reflect the category-wise breakup of the draft electoral rolls.
The Election Commission has also ordered a special drive to identify and enrol eligible voters who may have been left out during SIR.
